results.title: Performing
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “Job Catch”.
This film demonstrates ways in which an applicant can take a more positive role in a job interview by gaining a thorough understanding of the job interview process, thereby ensuring a more confident and relaxed attitude. Methods of utilising information on the nature of the job, and the work operations of the company or organisation are discussed, together with ways of improving performance in the job interview.

results.title: Performance appraisal: the human dynamics
results.brief_description: This film looks at the performance appraisal in everyday situations, including work. Dr. Alex Rosen, a specialist in organisational performance appraisal talks about the subject and sites that a number of organizations have experimented with a variety of performance appraisal systems, in an attempt to make a valuation of work performance a more productive experience.

results.title: Performance and development review. Part one
results.brief_description: Two scenarios are presented, the first one being a less than ideal setting for a performance appraisal review, and the second one a more favourable setting. In between the two sessions the tape poses questions, then reflects back on the interview in light of the issues raised. Issues covered include effective management styles, dynamics, opportunities, preparation, personal focus, and dealing with problems.

results.title: Perfect diet
results.brief_description: Jo Pearson of the Channel 10 Eyewitness News presents a special five-part news feature on diet. Episode 1. Examines the basics of the Australian Nutrition Foundation’s Perfect Diet Pyramid. Episode 2. Highlights the dietary problems of teenagers and children and analyses the Beverly Hills diet. Episode 3. Looks at how fat assessment is carried out and the myth of cellulite. Provides an analysis of Dr. Atkins diet. Episode 4. Shows the characteristics of diets that make people fat and analyses the F-Plan diet. Episode 5. Examines the myths of dieting: e.g. honey is better than sugar, bread and potatoes are fattening and analyses the Scarsdale diet. No other credits available.

results.brief_description: The timpani, snare drum, cymbals, tambourine, castanets, triangle, and celesta, underline the rhythm in music. results.title: Percussion group
results.creator_credit: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films and ERPI Classroom Films
results.brief_description: More than a dozen of the more commonly used percussion instruments are demonstrated. Chief attention is given to the structure, manner of tuning and playing of the tympani. Other percussion instruments represented are the tom-tom, snare drum, bass drum, tambourine, gong cymbals, castanets, triangle bells, celeste, chimes and the xylophone. Included into the compositions used are portions of Schubert’s “March Militaire” and of Tchaikovsky’s “Fourth Symphony”. Demonstrations throughout are given in full orchestral setting.
